Data preparation

Source: vignettes/vg01-prepare-data.Rmd
vg01-prepare-data.Rmd

spifa() expects data in a specific shape: one row per respondent, and the binary item responses stored as a single matrix-valued column (nobs x nitems) rather than one column per item. This is the same convention base R uses for multivariate lm(). This vignette builds a small dataset acceptable by spifa().

library(spifa)
library(sf)
#> Linking to GEOS 3.12.1, GDAL 3.8.4, PROJ 9.4.0; sf_use_s2() is TRUE

Simulating a raw questionnaire

Five binary items, a household wealth covariate, and GPS coordinates, for 20 households:

set.seed(1)
nobs <- 20
nitems <- 5

raw <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(nobs),
  wealth = rnorm(nobs),
  lon = runif(nobs, -71.70, -71.68),
  lat = runif(nobs, -7.06, -7.04),
  item1 = rbinom(nobs, 1, 0.1) == 1,
  item2 = rbinom(nobs, 1, 0.2) == 1,
  item3 = rbinom(nobs, 1, 0.3) == 1,
  item4 = rbinom(nobs, 1, 0.4) == 1,
  item5 = rbinom(nobs, 1, 0.5) == 1
)
raw

Data for spifa()

We extract the item as a matrix, and then provide it to a new data.frame to later convert to sf:

# get items as a matrix
items <- subset(raw, select = grep("^item", names(raw))) |>
  as.matrix() |>
  unname()
# create data.frame and geo-reference it
data <- data.frame(items = I(items), wealth = raw$wealth, x = raw$lon, y = raw$lat) |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326)
data
#> Simple feature collection with 20 features and 2 fields

This dataset can directly be used to fit a model:

spifa(items ~ wealth, data = data, nfactors = 2, niter = 5)

Alternatively, you could also create the sf data first and then assign the items:

data <- data.frame(wealth = raw$wealth, x = raw$lon, y = raw$lat) |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326)
data$items <- items
data

Missing values

Missing item responses

Individual missing item responses (NA) don’t need to be dropped or imputed – spifa() handles them natively, treating a missing response as an unobserved auxiliary variable to be sampled along with everything else, rather than requiring complete rows:

data_na <- data
data_na$items[1:5, 1] <- NA

fit_na <- spifa(items ~ 1, data = data_na, nfactors = 2, ngp = 0, niter = 5)
fit_na
#> Item factor analysis model: eifa
#> Formula: items ~ 1
#> Dimensions: 20 respondents, 5 items, 2 latent factors, 0 spatial processes
#> MCMC: 1 chain, iter = 5, thin = 1, samples = 5
#> 
#> Item model parameters:
#>         mean median   sd     q10   q90 ess_bulk rhat
#> c[1]   -0.76 -0.759 0.41 -1.1637 -0.35       NA  1.9

As you can see in Dimensions, the missing responses are not removed but rather modelled.

Missing predictor values

Missing predictor values behave differently, and are worth calling out: a NA in a predictor column drops that respondent from the whole fit:

data_na <- data
data_na$wealth[1:5] <- NA

fit_na <- spifa(items ~ wealth, data = data_na, nfactors = 2, ngp = 0, niter = 5)
fit_na
#> Item factor analysis model: cifa_pred
#> Formula: items ~ wealth
#> Dimensions: 15 respondents, 5 items, 2 latent factors, 0 spatial processes
